title: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03) - Intermediate

summary.description: Intermediate scenarios requiring solid AWS knowledge and multi-service integration patterns.

questions.question: A global e-commerce company processes 2TB of transaction data daily across 15 regions. Their current architecture uses RDS Multi-AZ in each region with cross-region read replicas, but they're experiencing 3-second query response times during peak hours (Black Friday sales). The company needs to maintain ACID compliance, support complex analytical queries, and ensure data consistency across all regions. They also want to reduce costs by 40% while improving performance. Which approach should they implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Implement Aurora Global Database with Aurora Serverless v2 for auto-scaling and use ElastiCache for Redis with cross-region replication
choices.explanation: Correct — Aurora Global Database provides ACID compliance, cross-region consistency, and Aurora Serverless v2 auto-scales during peak times. ElastiCache for Redis with cross-region replication provides sub-millisecond caching for frequently accessed data, reducing query response times while maintaining data consistency.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Migrate to DynamoDB Global Tables with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) and implement DynamoDB Streams for real-time analytics
choices.explanation: Incorrect — While DynamoDB Global Tables provide global replication, DynamoDB doesn't support complex analytical queries or ACID transactions required for e-commerce financial data.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deploy Redshift clusters in each region with cross-region data synchronization and use Redshift Spectrum for complex queries
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Redshift is designed for analytical workloads and doesn't provide the ACID compliance or real-time transactional capabilities required for e-commerce operations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Implement RDS Proxy with read replicas across regions and use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with custom sharding
choices.explanation: Incorrect — RDS Proxy helps with connection pooling but doesn't address the fundamental performance issues. Memcached doesn't provide the data consistency guarantees needed for financial transactions.

questions.question: A financial services company needs to implement a zero-trust security architecture across 50 AWS accounts in their organization. They must ensure that all data flows are encrypted in transit and at rest, implement least-privilege access, and maintain audit trails for compliance. The company processes sensitive financial data and must meet PCI DSS, SOX, and GDPR requirements. Which comprehensive approach should they implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploy IAM policies with resource-based policies and security groups with NACLs across all accounts
choices.explanation: Incorrect — While IAM policies and security groups are important, they don't provide comprehensive zero-trust architecture with encryption, audit trails, and compliance monitoring required for financial services.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deploy AWS WAF with Shield Advanced and AWS Firewall Manager for centralized security policy management
choices.explanation: Incorrect — WAF and Shield provide application-layer protection and DDoS mitigation but don't address the comprehensive zero-trust requirements including encryption, access control, and compliance monitoring.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Implement AWS Organizations with SCPs, AWS KMS for encryption, AWS CloudTrail for audit trails, AWS Config for compliance monitoring, and VPC endpoints for private connectivity
choices.explanation: Correct — This provides comprehensive zero-trust architecture: SCPs enforce least-privilege access, KMS ensures encryption, CloudTrail provides audit trails, Config monitors compliance, and VPC endpoints ensure private connectivity without internet exposure.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Implement VPC peering with Transit Gateway and AWS PrivateLink for secure inter-account communication
choices.explanation: Incorrect — While VPC peering and PrivateLink provide secure connectivity, they don't address the comprehensive zero-trust requirements including encryption, audit trails, and compliance monitoring.

questions.question: A healthcare company needs to implement a multi-region active-active disaster recovery solution for their patient data system. They must maintain HIPAA compliance, ensure data consistency across regions, and achieve RTO of 15 minutes and RPO of 5 minutes. The system processes 100,000 patient records daily and must support real-time data synchronization. Which approach should they implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploy RDS Multi-AZ with cross-region read replicas and implement custom application-level failover logic
choices.explanation: Incorrect — RDS read replicas don't provide true active-active capabilities and custom failover logic may not meet the strict RTO requirements for healthcare data.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deploy S3 with cross-region replication and CloudFront with Lambda@Edge for data processing
choices.explanation: Incorrect — S3 is object storage and doesn't provide the transactional database capabilities needed for patient data systems, even with Lambda@Edge processing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Implement Aurora Global Database with Aurora Serverless v2 and custom health check endpoints
choices.explanation: Incorrect — While Aurora Global Database provides cross-region replication, it may not meet the strict RTO requirements without additional failover mechanisms and doesn't provide true active-active capabilities.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Implement DynamoDB Global Tables with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) and use Route 53 health checks for automatic failover
choices.explanation: Correct — DynamoDB Global Tables provide active-active replication with eventual consistency, DAX provides sub-millisecond caching, and Route 53 health checks enable automatic failover to meet RTO requirements while maintaining HIPAA compliance.

questions.question: A gaming company needs to implement a global, low-latency architecture for their real-time multiplayer game that supports 1 million concurrent players. The game requires sub-50ms latency, real-time data synchronization, and must handle sudden traffic spikes during game launches. They also need to optimize costs while maintaining performance. Which approach should they implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Implement AWS Global Accelerator with Application Load Balancers in multiple regions, ElastiCache for Redis with cross-region replication, and DynamoDB Global Tables for real-time data
choices.explanation: Correct — Global Accelerator provides low-latency routing to multiple regions, ALBs distribute traffic, ElastiCache provides sub-millisecond caching for game state, and DynamoDB Global Tables ensure real-time data synchronization across regions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deploy EC2 instances in a single region with Application Load Balancer and implement custom client-side prediction
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Single region doesn't provide global low-latency access and won't handle 1 million concurrent players effectively, even with client-side prediction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deploy CloudFront with Lambda@Edge for game logic and S3 with intelligent tiering for data storage
choices.explanation: Incorrect — CloudFront with Lambda@Edge is designed for content delivery and edge computing, not for real-time multiplayer game architecture that requires persistent connections and dynamic data synchronization.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Implement Lambda functions with API Gateway and DynamoDB with on-demand capacity for game state management
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Lambda functions have cold start latency and execution time limits that make them unsuitable for real-time multiplayer games requiring consistent sub-50ms response times.

questions.question: A manufacturing company needs to implement a complex cost optimization strategy across 200 AWS accounts. They want to achieve 60% cost reduction while maintaining performance and implementing automated cost controls. The company has variable workloads, predictable workloads, and batch processing jobs. They also need to track costs by department, project, and environment. Which comprehensive approach should they implement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploy On-Demand instances across all accounts with CloudWatch for monitoring and custom cost tracking dashboards
choices.explanation: Incorrect — On-Demand instances are the most expensive option and custom dashboards don't provide automated cost controls or the scale needed across 200 accounts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deploy Spot Instances with Spot Fleets and Auto Scaling groups across all accounts for maximum cost savings
choices.explanation: Incorrect — Spot Instances can be interrupted and aren't suitable for all workload types, especially production workloads that require consistent availability, even with Spot Fleets.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Implement S3 with intelligent tiering for all data storage and Lambda with provisioned concurrency for all compute workloads
choices.explanation: Incorrect — This approach doesn't address the diverse workload requirements and may not provide optimal cost savings for all use cases, especially for workloads that don't benefit from serverless architectures.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Implement AWS Organizations with consolidated billing, use Reserved Instances for predictable workloads, Spot Instances for batch jobs, Savings Plans for variable workloads, and implement cost allocation tags with AWS Budgets and Cost Explorer
choices.explanation: Correct — This provides comprehensive cost optimization: Organizations enables consolidated billing and volume discounts, RIs for predictable workloads, Spot for batch jobs, Savings Plans for variable workloads, and cost allocation tags with Budgets/Explorer for automated monitoring and control.

questions.question: A media streaming company needs to implement a global content delivery network that can handle 100TB of video content daily with 99.99% availability. choices.explanation: Incorrect — While DynamoDB can store metadata and S3 can store files, this approach doesn't provide the CDN capabilities, live streaming support, or adaptive bitrate streaming needed for media delivery.
